quote.text: THIS MEASURE GIVES SAN FRANCISCO VOTERS THE OPPORTUNITY TO DECIDE WHETHER A TRANSFER TAX CODE SHOULD REFLECT THE WAY TODAY'S REAL ESTATE MARKET OPERATES RATHER THAN THE MARKET THAT EXISTED DECADES AGO.

statement.section: Proposition J — Removal of Foreclosure Exemption for Real Property Transfer Tax
statement.text: The exemption was written in 1967 for a bank stuck with a building it never wanted, and for decades it mostly covered homes. Then investors learned to buy the loan instead of the building, and the Assessor now counts $450M in foreclosure exemptions claimed in the last three years, against $50M in the fifteen years before that. The tax they skip is the one every ordinary buyer pays, and homes and small buildings keep the exemption either way.

reading.in_common: Same measure and same subject: the foreclosure exemption in the real property transfer tax (Prop J) and how the market has changed since the exemption was written.
reading.differs: Same side on the text: the quote presents the measure as bringing the transfer tax code up to date, and the donor's statement is on its page for Prop J, labelled 'Yes'. (My reading of the quote; the label is on the donor's page.)
